subject: Deployment mode & compliance follow-up: Acme Health (HIPAA / BAA / SOC2)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode & compliance follow-up: Acme Health (HIPAA / BAA / SOC2)

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on what we discussed: 

Summary of needs (from call):
- PHI in transit and at-rest for our pilot workflows; customer data residency in US.
- Formal BAA and SOC2 evidence for security and controls review.
- Preference for isolation and predictable throughput if we move beyond pilot (potentially Dedicated or Private).

Recommended path from Redwood:
1) Pilot on Hosted API under a BAA (short-term): faster to start, we can enable account-level isolation and token-level logging.
2) If throughput / isolation needs increase, evaluate Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity) — predictable latency and data isolation.
3) For ultimate control (on-prem or VPC with customer-managed networking) we can discuss Redwood Private — typical for regulated production deployments.

Attachments I shared in the call: SOC2 summary, a draft BAA, and a short deployment-mode matrix comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Links/attachments included below.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll send the SOC2 Type II summary + BAA draft (attached).
- Can you confirm whether Acme requires full on-prem hosting or if VPC (customer-managed networking) is sufficient?
- If procurement requires it, we can start a DocuSign BAA and schedule a technical evidence call with Dylan for next week.

Open questions for Acme:
- Expected RPS (requests per second) and peak concurrency for the pilot?
- Any additional compliance requirements beyond HIPAA/SOC2 (e.g., specific audit scopes)?

Happy to hop on another short call to align with your security and procurement teams.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_SOC2_Type2_summary_2025.pdf, BAA-draft-AcmeHealth.docx, deployment-mode-matrix.xlsx

From: Alex Green <alex.green@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & compliance follow-up: Acme Health (HIPAA / BAA / SOC2)

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the attachments: 

1) BAA: Procurement would like the BAA redlined and routed to our legal. Would you send as a Word doc (we received the docx) and a DocuSign link?
2) SOC2: Your SOC2 summary is great. Our security team will want the Type II report and the auditor letter. Can Dylan share the full Type II report or an auditor statement?
3) Deployment mode: For the pilot, we prefer Hosted API if it meets HIPAA + BAA controls — faster to get started. For longer term, if we see PII/PHI throughput above ~150 RPS or sustained latency needs, we will likely need Dedicated capacity. We do NOT plan to go fully on-prem unless mandated by a downstream regulator.

Operational asks: 
- Can you confirm data retention defaults and our ability to control retention / delete logs?
- Do you provide per-tenant encryption keys (KMS) or customer-managed keys for Dedicated / Private?

We'd like to schedule a short technical evidence call with your security engineering — can you do early next week (Mon/Tue)? Procurement copied on this thread.

Thanks,
Alex
VP, Product & Integration
Acme Health
alex.green@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2027 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & compliance follow-up: Acme Health (HIPAA / BAA / SOC2)

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Confirming each point and next actions below.

1) BAA + DocuSign: I've attached the Word copy (same as before) and will generate a DocuSign envelope this afternoon and share the link. If Acme needs redlines, we can accept tracked changes and have our legal review quickly.

2) SOC2 evidence: Dylan — can you confirm whether we can share the full SOC2 Type II report and the auditor letter for Acme's security review? If not, what is the minimal auditor statement we can provide?

3) Data retention & KMS: short answers — we support configurable retention windows at account level for logs and KV caches; for Hosted we manage keys by default but we can offer customer-managed keys (via KMS) for Dedicated and Private. I'll attach the retention defaults in the deployment-matrix.

4) Pilot mode: Hosted under BAA is viable and will reduce time-to-first-test. If Acme determines sustained RPS >150 or requires guaranteed latency SLOs, recommended move is Dedicated. Private is a later-stage option if regulators insist on on-prem.

Proposed next steps:
- I'll send DocuSign BAA link by EOD.
- Dylan — can you propose two 30-min slots Mon/Tue next week for the technical evidence call (SOC2 + architecture)?
- Alex/procurement — please confirm preferred time and any extra attendees for the call (security lead, cloud infra, legal).

Marissa

Attachments: BAA-draft-AcmeHealth.docx (attached again), deployment-mode-matrix.xlsx

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & compliance follow-up: Acme Health (HIPAA / BAA / SOC2)

Alex / team — happy to run the technical evidence session. We can provide: full SOC2 Type II report under NDA, auditor letter, and a scoped evidence bundle (network diagrams, encryption controls, key rotation policy, access control lists).

Proposed 30-min slots:
- Mon, 07 Jun 2027 at 09:30 - 10:00 PT
- Tue, 08 Jun 2027 at 14:00 - 14:30 PT

Notes on hosting modes re: your asks:
- Hosted (under BAA): supports account-level data isolation, configurable retention; default key management is Redwood-managed KMS; customer-managed keys available as an add-on for higher tiers.
- Dedicated: customer-dedicated GPU pools with options for customer-managed KMS and stricter network isolation (VPC peering).
- Private: full customer VPC or on-prem; we can support HSM integrations and dedicated audit trails.

I'll prepare the SOC2 docs for sharing; we usually require an NDA for the full report; if Acme prefers, we can provide an auditor letter / attest first.

Dylan Brooks
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
